Bright.

Demand currently outstrips supply. Acoustics is a small market and demand isn’t huge, but the pool of good candidates is even smaller. I’ve seen lots of companies, in China and abroad, struggle to find a suitable acoustics engineer.

Manufacturing has hit a plateau, and people-centered design is getting more and more attention. Take the automotive industry: there isn’t a carmaker today that isn’t hiring NVH people, and every department needs them. The demands of the OEMs, the big daddies of the industry, drive the whole supply chain, so suppliers at every tier are piling in too. They have to, or the big daddies won’t be happy!

People who can code are a dime a dozen; people who understand acoustics are few and far between.

By understanding acoustics I don’t just mean being able to calculate a sound pressure level and add A-weighting, or using a sound level meter and naming a few damping materials. At the very least, you should know the Helmholtz equation, have read a few of the basic textbooks, have done some related research and be able to read academic papers.


I’ll come back and say more when I have time.

Fanyu Meng · 108 consultations · rated 5.0 · Zhihu outstanding answerer in acoustics · PhD in acoustics, RWTH Aachen University
